name.common: Founding of Cairo as the new capital of Egypt
meaningOfNames: Cairo is derived from the Arabic name 'Al-Qāhirah', meaning 'The Victorious'.
longFormInfo: The founding of Cairo marked a significant shift in the political and cultural landscape of Egypt.
Cairo was founded in 969 CE by the Fatimid dynasty.

significance: The founding of Cairo established it as a major political, cultural, and economic centre in the Islamic world.
legacy: Cairo has evolved into one of the largest and most influential cities in the Arab world, with a rich history that continues to shape its identity.
shortSummary: Cairo was founded in 969 CE by the Fatimid dynasty as the new capital of Egypt.
longSummary: The founding of Cairo was a pivotal moment in Egyptian history, as it replaced Fustat as the capital and became a centre of Islamic learning and culture.
Cairo's strategic location along the Nile River facilitated trade and communication, contributing to its rapid growth and development.
Over the centuries, Cairo has witnessed significant historical events and has been home to numerous dynasties, making it a melting pot of cultures and traditions.

participants.name: Jawhar al-Siqilli
participants.role: Fatimid general who conquered Egypt and laid out the city

participants.name: al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah
participants.role: Fatimid caliph who ordered it and moved his court there in 973
